theme: Third-party dependency risk — vulnerable (direct, transitive, test-only), deprecated, outdated, copyleft and end-of-life platform — and their look-alikes, in a small .NET invoice-rendering service, worker and legacy exporter

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: Newtonsoft.Json
entries.rationale: NuGet Newtonsoft.Json 12.0.3, direct dependency of Invoicing.Api (it parses the legacy ERP webhook payload). Affected by GHSA-5crp-9r3c-p9vr / CVE-2024-21907 (high: improper handling of exceptional conditions; deeply nested JSON exhausts the stack and kills the process), fixed in 13.0.1 (osv.dev: introduced 0, fixed 13.0.1). The webhook endpoint parses caller-supplied JSON with JObject.Parse, so the vulnerable path is on an internet-facing request.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: SharpZipLib
entries.rationale: NuGet SharpZipLib 1.3.2, direct dependency of the archive exporter (a shipped command-line tool), which writes the yearly archive ZIP with it. Affected by GHSA-m22m-h4rf-pwq3 / CVE-2021-32840 (high), GHSA-2x7h-96h5-rq84 / CVE-2021-32841 and GHSA-mm6g-mmq6-53ff / CVE-2021-32842, all path traversal on extraction and all fixed in 1.3.3 (osv.dev: introduced 0, fixed 1.3.3). The exporter only writes archives today, so the vulnerable extraction path is not reached; the concept is the affected version, which this is, and the fix is a minor-version bump.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: SixLabors.ImageSharp
entries.rationale: TRANSITIVE: NuGet SixLabors.ImageSharp 1.0.4, never declared by this repository, resolved because the direct dependency PdfSharpCore 1.3.67 (the current release) declares SixLabors.ImageSharp >= 1.0.4 and NuGet picks the lowest version the range admits. ImageSharp 1.0.4 is affected by seven published advisories, among them GHSA-65x7-c272-7g7r / CVE-2024-27929 (use after free, fixed 2.1.7), GHSA-63p8-c4ww-9cg7 / CVE-2024-41131 (out-of-bounds write, fixed 2.1.9) and GHSA-2cmq-823j-5qj8 / CVE-2025-27598 (out-of-bounds write, fixed 2.1.10) (osv.dev). The renderer feeds customer-uploaded logos through PdfSharpCore's XImage, which decodes them with ImageSharp. The site is the resolved entry in the lock file of the project that declares PdfSharpCore; the fix is a central transitive pin or a direct reference to a patched ImageSharp.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: SharpCompress
entries.rationale: NuGet SharpCompress 0.28.3, referenced ONLY by the unit-test project (it opens the exporter's ZIP output to assert its contents). Affected by GHSA-jp7f-grcv-6mjf / CVE-2021-39208 (partial path traversal, fixed 0.29) and GHSA-6c8g-7p36-r338 / CVE-2026-44788 (directory traversal via directory entries in WriteTo, fixed 0.48.0) (osv.dev). Decided as a must-fire, not a trap: the concept is 'a declared or locked package version affected by a published advisory' and carries no scope; the package is declared, locked, restored and executed on every CI run, on runners that hold repository tokens. It is LOWER RISK than a shipped dependency (fixture input only, nothing shipped), which changes its priority, not whether it is true.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: Polly.Extensions.Http
entries.rationale: NuGet Polly.Extensions.Http 3.0.0 (the last release), direct dependency of Invoicing.Api for the logo client's retry policy. nuget.org deprecation metadata on every version: reason 'Legacy', alternate package Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience. No advisory: this is deprecation only.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: CsvHelper
entries.rationale: NuGet CsvHelper 12.1.2, published 2019-01-28, direct dependency of the archive exporter. The current release is 33.1.0 (2025-06-02): 21 major versions and more than six years behind. No advisory and no deprecation (osv.dev and nuget.org metadata checked 2026-10-07): pure staleness, which is what makes it the outdated-only plant.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: MySql.Data
entries.rationale: NuGet MySql.Data 26.7.0, direct dependency of Invoicing.Worker, licence expression 'GPL-2.0-only WITH Universal-FOSS-exception-1.0' (nuspec). The worker ships in the customer-installed bundle under a proprietary licence (docs/adr/0003-third-party-licence-policy.md); the policy forbids GPL-family licences in any shipped component, and the Universal FOSS Exception only covers combination with FOSS-licensed software, which a proprietary bundle is not. Oracle sells a commercial Connector/NET licence for exactly this case; none is recorded.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.subject: net6.0
entries.rationale: The archive exporter is an executable whose only target framework is net6.0, and the next line switches off the SDK's own end-of-life warning (CheckEolTargetFramework=false). .NET 6 LTS reached end of support on 2024-11-12 (Microsoft release metadata, dotnetcli releases-index.json: eol-date 2024-11-12): the runtime it runs on receives no security patches.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: System.Security.Cryptography.Xml
entries.rationale: NuGet System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 10.0.12 (XML-DSig for the signed e-invoice). The package has a long advisory record: GHSA-vh55-786g-wjwj / CVE-2022-34716 (fixed 4.7.1 / 6.0.1), and five 2026 advisories against the 10.0 line (GHSA-cvvh-rhrc-wg4q, GHSA-g8r8-53c2-pm3f, GHSA-23rf-6693-g89p, GHSA-8q5v-6pqq-x66h, GHSA-mmjf-rqrv-855v: introduced 10.0.0, fixed 10.0.10). 10.0.12 is past every fix; osv.dev returns no advisory for 10.0.12. A matcher that keys on the package name, or on a version prefix, is caught.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: MailKit
entries.rationale: NuGet MailKit 4.18.1 (resolving MimeKit 4.18.1), used by the worker to send the rendered invoice. Both packages carry 2026 advisories against earlier versions: MailKit GHSA-9j88-vvj5-vhgr / CVE-2026-41319 (STARTTLS response injection, fixed 4.16.0) and MimeKit GHSA-g7hc-96xr-gvvx / CVE-2026-30227 (CRLF injection, fixed 4.15.1). The pinned versions are patched; osv.dev returns nothing for either.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: iTextSharp.LGPLv2.Core
entries.rationale: NuGet iTextSharp.LGPLv2.Core 3.8.6, licence expression LGPL-2.0-only, used unmodified by the archive exporter to stamp archived PDFs. Two ways to be fooled: the NAME (iTextSharp is widely known as AGPL; this is the LGPL fork of the last pre-AGPL code line) and a substring rule that bans 'GPL-2.0' and therefore matches 'LGPL-2.0-only'. The policy (docs/adr/0003-third-party-licence-policy.md) allows LGPL-2.0/2.1 for unmodified libraries consumed as separate assemblies, which a NuGet package loaded at run time is: the end user can replace the DLL.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: FluentAssertions
entries.rationale: NuGet FluentAssertions 7.2.2, test-only. 8.x exists, but from 8.0 the package is under a commercial licence (Xceed); 7.x stays Apache-2.0 and is still maintained (7.2.1 2026-02-07, 7.2.2 2026-03-16). Staying on the 7 line is a recorded decision (docs/adr/0004-stay-on-fluentassertions-7.md) and 7.2.2 is the newest release of that line: current within its line, pinned by design, no advisory.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: Bogus
entries.rationale: NuGet Bogus 35.6.5, test-only fake-data generator (bchavez/Bogus, MIT, 35 major versions, the standard .NET port of faker.js). The name reads like a warning; the package is not in any malicious-package feed (no MAL- or CWE-506 record on osv.dev). A name or keyword heuristic is caught.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: netstandard2.0
entries.rationale: The contracts library multi-targets netstandard2.0 and net10.0 so that the customer's ERP connector (.NET Framework 4.8) can reference it. .NET Standard is a specification, not a runtime, and has no end-of-support date; the library runs on net10.0 (supported to 2028-11-14) everywhere this repository runs it. Neither target is an end-of-life platform.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.subject: Cronos
entries.rationale: NuGet Cronos 0.13.0 (MIT, HangfireIO/Cronos), the worker's cron-expression parser. A 0.x version number reads as unfinished, but 0.13.0 is a STABLE release: it carries no SemVer pre-release label, nuget.org lists it as the latest stable version (2026-04-29), and the project has shipped 0.x releases for years. A rule that equates 0.x with pre-release is caught. No advisory, not deprecated, current.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: CA2007 (ConfigureAwait) is switched off for the repository root, and the reason is on the line directly above it: tests must not use ConfigureAwait(false) (xUnit1030); src/.editorconfig and tools/.editorconfig switch CA2007 back on as a warning for all production code. A documented, scoped suppression is not a defect. Promoted from scan iteration 1 (a scanner reported it as unexplained), as in bench-csharp-baseline-clean TRP-001.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Central Package Management (Directory.Packages.props) and a committed packages.lock.json for every project, the net6.0 exporter included; CI restores in locked mode. The dependencies are pinned and reproducible even though several pinned versions are bad.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Actions are pinned by commit SHA, but the repository publishes no release artifact, so there is nothing to sign or attest and no SBOM; partial posture by design, wide band (same reasoning as bench-csharp-baseline-clean).

entries.rationale: Certified free of the dependency, licence, end-of-life-platform and CI/image-pinning concepts this repository covers (whole file).
